title: Bounded constructible pro-etale complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ be the derived category of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$ let $\mathcal H^i(K)$ be its $i$-th cohomology sheaf [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $P$ be the property of $K$: $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, and every $\mathcal H^i(K)$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[n]$ does, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Pro-etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 61.27.3 (Tag 09AL, label lemma-compare-constructible-derived), from Lemma 61.27.2 (Tag 09B5, label lemma-constructible-serre: constructible sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory) and Derived Categories, Section 13.17 (Tag 06UP), Lemma Tag 06UQ (label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, bounded version); also literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Definition 1.1 (3)

proof.text: Constructible sheaves contain every zero object. Use the single stratum Y with identity immersion. The constant coefficient comparison is an isomorphism: compose the constant-sheaf adjunction with inverse image, identify its right adjoint with evaluation on the terminal base-changed object, and use uniqueness of left adjoints. Applying the composite adjunction hom-equivalence identifies its isomorphism with the specified coefficient map, because both maps have the same constant-section normalization. Thus the displayed constant-module pullback is the existing exact operations functor specialized along this coefficient isomorphism, and it sends zero to zero. The identity covering trivializes zero with the zero constant module. Its geometric stalk is zero, since restriction preserves zero maps and the stalk colimit is a left adjoint, so its underlying set is finite. A sheaf isomorphism transports the same finite partition: module pullback is functorial, localization sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms, and stalk isomorphisms are bijections of underlying sets. Hence the constructible class is closed under isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof of Tag 09AL, label lemma-compare-constructible-derived: identify the ambient module category and the constructible cohomology class.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-proetale-constructible-exact-closure] to get constructibility of the selected kernel and cokernel and of the middle term of any short exact sequence. Any other limiting kernel or colimiting cokernel is uniquely isomorphic to the selected one. Isomorphism closure from the preceding step transports constructibility along these comparison isomorphisms. These are exactly the three ObjectProperty weak-Serre closure classes.

The ambient proEtaleRingModules category is the Mathlib abelian category SheafOfModules, and its derived category and homology are the specified DerivedCategory constructions. Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to the constructible object property P, using zero and isomorphism closure from step 1 and kernel, cokernel and extension closure from step 2. Its bounded clause gives ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated for homologyProperty P intersected with the bounded standard derived class.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including its bounded versions; this is the general result used in the proof of Tag 09AL.

proof.text: For a complex K let T be the set of integer degrees with nonzero homology. Mathlib Set.finite_iff_bddBelow_bddAbove says T is finite iff it has lower and upper bounds. DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff identify these bounds with vanishing of homology below and above the respective integers, so finite support is exactly membership in the standard bounded subcategory. Pointwise conjunction commutes, hence the predicate in the statement equals homologyProperty P intersected with the bounded predicate. Substitute this equality into the bounded triangulated conclusion of the preceding step and its isomorphism-closure instance.
